subject: Post-call: Pricing & latency trade-offs / token volume confirmation

Subject: Post-call: Pricing & latency trade-offs / token volume confirmation

Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment.

Key items we discussed:
- Expected monthly token volume: ~15M–25M tokens (peak month could be ~40M).
- Latency target: 300–600ms P95 for chat responses (some endpoints can tolerate streaming).
- Primary constraint: keep unit cost below your internal target (~$800–$1,200 per 1M tokens) to hit your product economics.
- Risk areas: higher context windows (2k–8k tokens) for some flows will increase CPU/GPU work; heavy concurrency during batch jobs.

Next steps (agreed on call):
1) Samir to confirm the distribution between short (<=256 token) vs long (1k–8k token) requests — we said you'd share a sample volume breakdown.
2) We (Redwood) to propose two pricing buckets: (a) latency-optimized (SLO-backed, higher unit cost) and (b) cost-optimized (batching/caching encouraged, lower unit cost).
3) Rishi to sketch recommended batch settings / streaming options and expected per-1M-token price deltas.
4) We'll produce a one-page comparison + ballpark pricing and an initial SOW draft.

I attached a first-pass "redwood-pricing-options.pdf" and a template token-volume CSV — please drop the numbers in and we’ll update.

If anything above is off, flag it. Otherwise, comment on the attached CSV with your volume split and we’ll run numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0187

Subject: Re: Post-call: Pricing & latency trade-offs / token volume confirmation

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications and the volume split attached.

Quick answers:
- Monthly baseline we expect ~18M tokens. During large batch runs (end of month reconciliation) we can spike to ~42M tokens.
- Distribution in the CSV (attached): 72% short requests (<=256 tokens), 20% medium (257–1024), 8% long (1k–8k).
- Budget: we are targeting total monthly inference spend of $14k–$18k to start (scalable). That implies a target unit cost around $777–$1,000 per 1M tokens depending on how we measure (we understand latency tradeoffs may push cost up).
- Latency: For the main customer-facing chat flow we need P95 <= 500ms; background workflows (batch reranks / embeddings) can be 1.5–3s. We prefer streaming for long responses to improve perceived latency.

Requests: can you show us two scenarios with numbers:
A) Latency-first (P95 <= 300–400ms) with expected $/1M tokens and likely capacity commitment needed.
B) Cost-first (allow batching, P95 ~600–800ms, aggressive caching) with $/1M tokens.

Elisa — looping you for procurement and any questions on compliance; Samir and I can sync on the CSV.

Samir
Head of Product, FintechAI
samir@fintechai.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Pricing & latency trade-offs / token volume confirmation

Perfect — thanks for the CSV, that helps a lot. High-level reaction before Rishi drops the math:

- Given 72% short requests, aggressive batching and caching will reduce your effective unit cost on those tokens substantially. Short-turn chat tokens are where batching has the least upside (since latency is critical) so we’ll separate pricing by route.
- For the long/streaming responses (8% of volume) we recommend streaming to preserve perceived latency; this increases resource time slightly but often improves UX without needing the highest tier.
- Baseline ask: can you confirm whether the $14k–$18k budget is a hard cap for Q2 trial or a stretchy target if SLA-backed pricing is necessary? That will change whether we steer you toward Dedicated reserved capacity vs Hosted with committed usage.

I’ll let Rishi add the concrete $/1M numbers for both scenarios (latency-first vs cost-first) and a recommended tier (Hosted Standard / Hosted Plus / Dedicated) for each.

Thanks — attaching a short SLO/pricing explainer and the proposed-sla-tiering.docx for reference.

Marissa

Subject: RE: Post-call: Pricing & latency trade-offs / token volume confirmation

Thanks — did the quick math based on the CSV attached. Summary (ballpark):

Scenario A — Latency-first (P95 <= 300–400ms)
- Recommended: Hosted Plus (SLA-backed), or Dedicated if you want guaranteed tail latency under concurrent spikes.
- Expected unit cost: ~$1,200–$1,450 per 1M tokens (higher because we prioritize single-request placement, minimal batching, and GPU with faster kernels).
- Capacity note: to hit P95 targets during spikes you’d need a committed buffer (~1.5x baseline peak). We can show exact GPU count in the SOW.

Scenario B — Cost-first (P95 ~600–800ms)
- Recommended: Hosted Standard with aggressive batching + prefix caching; Dedicated if you expect consistent high throughput and want lower per-token pricing.
- Expected unit cost: ~$650–$900 per 1M tokens (savings driven by batching and KV/prefix caching; long responses served via streaming to reduce perceived latency).

Hybrid recommendation:
- Start Hosted Standard with a committed monthly commit that gives you cost protection, and enable an autoscaler with a short-powered burst policy. After two months of real traffic, move hot routes to Dedicated for predictable tail latency.

Attachments I’ll provide after this thread: a one-pager with the two-scenario numbers, and a short capacity sketch. For procurement — if your budget is a hard cap at $14k/month, we’ll model a conservative Hosted Standard plan to stay within spend but it will likely increase the P95 to ~650–800ms on peak.

Numbers caveats: these are ballparks; exact per-1M token pricing depends on your route split, context window distribution, and effective cache hit ratio. We’ll run the actual workload through our cost model once we have the CSV filled (thanks).

Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the SOW draft.

Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
